findings.issue_text: **`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35-36` — Stored XSS via unsanitized RSS/Atom feed content.**

`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is passed straight into `TopicEmbed.import` with no tag/attribute whitelisting. `TopicEmbed.import` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb:10-42`) does no sanitization either — it only rewrites relative URLs via `absolutize_urls` — and stores the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` (`app/models/post.rb:130-137`) short-circuits and returns `raw` unprocessed for `raw_html` posts, bypassing the normal PrettyText/whitelist sanitization pipeline entirely, and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (explicitly unescaped). A feed item containing `<script>`/`onerror=`/etc. will execute in the context of the forum's own domain for every visitor who views that topic (not just inside the sandboxed iframe embed) — this is a full stored-XSS chain reachable simply by pointing `feed_polling_url` at any feed that isn't fully trusted or that gets compromised.

Contrast this with `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb:44-53`), which at least passes `tags:`/`attributes:` whitelists to `Readability::Document.new` before calling `.import` — showing the authors were aware sanitization was needed for one path but omitted it on the other.

`Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` uses the open-uri-patched `Kernel#open`, which is a well-known Ruby foot-gun (strings beginning with `|` are executed as a shell pipe). The host-equality check in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` mitigates the most direct exploitation route today, but it's the only thing standing between untrusted input and `open()`, and it doesn't restrict scheme — `import_remote`'s network fetch happens *before* the `^https?://` check in `TopicEmbed.import` (`topic_embed.rb:11`) is ever reached. Prefer `URI.parse(url).open`/explicit scheme allow-listing before fetching, as defense in depth rather than relying solely on the host-match check.
**`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26` and `lib/topic_retriever.rb:15` — Access control keyed entirely on `Referer`.**
**`lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148` — Behavior regression in the Disqus importer.**

**`app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6` — `<%- end if %>` typo.** The stray trailing `if` is parsed as a modifier-if wrapping the preceding `if/else` block, which reorders evaluation so the whitespace between `end` and the next tag renders *before* the title/start_discussion link instead of after. It doesn't crash and is visually masked because `.logo` is `float: right` in `embed.css.scss`, but it's a real parser quirk that indicates the rendered output was never inspected. Should just be `<%- end %>`.

**`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17` — Weak postMessage origin check.** `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring match, not an exact-origin comparison. Impact is low (only gates iframe resize height), but should be `e.origin === discourseUrl` (or compare against `new URL(discourseUrl).origin`) rather than substring containment.
**`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-22` — Dead code.** `feed_key` is defined (looks like scaffolding for conditional-GET/If-Modified-Since caching) but never called anywhere in the class.

**`db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`** — unrelated `force: true` addition to an already-existing migration for `top_topics`, out of scope for an "embed URL handling" PR; edits to previously-shipped migrations are best avoided since they're a no-op wherever the migration already ran but silently change behavior for fresh installs.
**`config/locales/server.en.yml`** adds `embed.permalink: "Permalink"`, which is never referenced anywhere in the diff — dead i18n key.

**`app/models/topic_embed.rb:13` — mutates the caller's `contents` string via `<<`.** Works today because both call sites (`import_remote`, `poll_feed`) pass freshly-built strings, but it's a fragile side effect that could bite a future caller who passes a reused/frozen string.
**`app/models/topic_embed.rb:34-38`** — on re-poll, only the post body is revised; the topic *title* is never updated if the source article's title changes.

**`app/models/topic_embed.rb:25-28`** — `TopicEmbed.create!` inside the transaction isn't rescued; a race between two concurrent imports of the same `embed_url` (unique index collision) will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` all the way up to the Sidekiq job instead of being handled gracefully (e.g., re-fetch the winner's embed).

**Testing gap:** the only spec touching `PollFeed#poll_feed` mocks the method away entirely (`spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`), so the exact code path that has no HTML sanitization (the Critical finding above) has zero test coverage. A test asserting that dangerous markup from a feed item is stripped/escaped would have caught this.
Several new files are missing trailing newlines (`embed.css.scss`, `loading.html.erb`, `layouts/embed.html.erb`, `topic_retriever.rb`) — cosmetic only.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35-36` — Stored XSS via unsanitized RSS/Atom feed content.**

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` the job imports `i.content` from an external RSS/Atom feed (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` then creates a post with `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` and explicitly sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (and `skip_validations: true`). In `Post#cook`, `:raw_html` returns `raw` directly, skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Finally, the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any HTML/JS from the feed can be stored and executed when viewed. This is a verifiable stored XSS path introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is passed straight into `TopicEmbed.import` with no tag/attribute whitelisting. `TopicEmbed.import` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb:10-42`) does no sanitization either — it only rewrites relative URLs via `absolutize_urls` — and stores the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` (`app/models/post.rb:130-137`) short-circuits and returns `raw` unprocessed for `raw_html` posts, bypassing the normal PrettyText/whitelist sanitization pipeline entirely, and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (explicitly unescaped). A feed item containing `<script>`/`onerror=`/etc. will execute in the context of the forum's own domain for every visitor who views that topic (not just inside the sandboxed iframe embed) — this is a full stored-XSS chain reachable simply by pointing `feed_polling_url` at any feed that isn't fully trusted or that gets compromised.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an import path that deliberately stores and serves raw HTML without Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is passed to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and does not sanitize the HTML (it only appends an “imported from” footer and rewrites relative URLs in `absolutize_urls`). In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` short-circuits and returns `raw`, bypassing the rendering/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any `<script>` tags or event-handler attributes present in the feed content will be emitted as-is. Because this creates normal Discourse posts/topics (not just iframe-only content), this is a stored-XSS vector if `feed_polling_url` points at an untrusted/compromised feed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Contrast this with `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb:44-53`), which at least passes `tags:`/`attributes:` whitelists to `Readability::Document.new` before calling `.import` — showing the authors were aware sanitization was needed for one path but omitted it on the other.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the RSS/ATOM path (`Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` → `TopicEmbed.import`), `contents` from the feed is used essentially as raw HTML: it is only `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`’d and then passed through `absolutize_urls`, which only rewrites relative `href`/`src` values and does not sanitize/strip unsafe tags/attributes (e.g., `<script>`, `onerror`, `javascript:` URLs, etc.). The post is then created with `cook_method: :raw_html`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for that cook method, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline; the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. By contrast, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` constructs a `Readability::Document` with explicit `tags:`/`attributes:` allowlists before calling `import`. This is a real, verifiable security/correctness issue introduced by the diff (XSS risk via feed content).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In both `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the code compares hosts using direct string inequality (`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(...).host`). DNS hostnames are case-insensitive, but Ruby's `URI(...).host` preserves the original casing from the URL, and `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is a plain string. This can incorrectly reject otherwise valid embed URLs/referers when the same host is presented with different capitalization (e.g., `EvilTrout.com` vs `eviltrout.com`). Normalizing (e.g., `.downcase`) would avoid the false mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`** — unrelated `force: true` addition to an already-existing migration for `top_topics`, out of scope for an "embed URL handling" PR; edits to previously-shipped migrations are best avoided since they're a no-op wherever the migration already ran but silently change behavior for fresh installs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `force: true` to an existing migration (`create_table :top_topics, force: true`). However, this is primarily a scope/process concern (editing a previously-committed migration) rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the code. In normal operation, already-run migrations are not re-executed, so it’s a no-op for existing installs, and on a fresh install the table won’t exist yet so `force: true` doesn’t change behavior. While it could be risky if someone manually reruns the migration in a dirty DB where `top_topics` already exists, that’s a speculative/edge operational scenario, not a clear problem evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`config/locales/server.en.yml`** adds `embed.permalink: "Permalink"`, which is never referenced anywhere in the diff — dead i18n key.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `embed.permalink: "Permalink"` in `config/locales/server.en.yml`, and there is no reference to `t('embed.permalink')` (or similar) in any of the added/modified files shown. However, concluding it is a “dead i18n key” is not verifiable from this diff alone because the key could be referenced elsewhere in the codebase outside the displayed changes. At most, this is an unproven cleanup/nit rather than a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/models/topic_embed.rb:13` — mutates the caller's `contents` string via `<<`.** Works today because both call sites (`import_remote`, `poll_feed`) pass freshly-built strings, but it's a fragile side effect that could bite a future caller who passes a reused/frozen string.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` does mutate the passed-in String. However, within this diff there’s no verifiable bug or correctness/security issue caused by that mutation: the shown call sites (`PollFeed` builds `content` from feed data; `import_remote` uses `doc.content`) pass newly created, mutable strings and do not reuse them after the call. The claim that it’s “fragile” for future callers (or for frozen strings) is speculative and not demonstrably a defect introduced by this diff as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/models/topic_embed.rb:34-38`** — on re-poll, only the post body is revised; the topic *title* is never updated if the source article's title changes.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing `TopicEmbed` is found (`embed` present), the update path only revises the post raw via `PostRevisor#revise!` and updates `content_sha1`. The passed-in `title` argument is not used at all in this branch, and the update is gated solely by `content_sha1` (computed from `contents` only). Therefore, if the source article title changes (with or without content changes), the Discourse topic title will never be updated by re-polling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/models/topic_embed.rb:25-28`** — `TopicEmbed.create!` inside the transaction isn't rescued; a race between two concurrent imports of the same `embed_url` (unique index collision) will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` all the way up to the Sidekiq job instead of being handled gracefully (e.g., re-fetch the winner's embed).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-locking `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` check and then, if blank, proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. Since the migration adds a **unique index** on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, two concurrent callers importing the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and then race into `create!`, causing an `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`/unique constraint violation. There is no rescue/handling in the method, so the exception would propagate (e.g., out of `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` / `TopicRetriever`), failing the job instead of gracefully using the existing row.

In the added `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, there is indeed a `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` that is not referenced anywhere in that spec. However, this is primarily an unused/extra require (a cleanup/perf/style nit) and is not a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone unless the required file is missing (which is not shown in this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Testing gap:** the only spec touching `PollFeed#poll_feed` mocks the method away entirely (`spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`), so the exact code path that has no HTML sanitization (the Critical finding above) has zero test coverage. A test asserting that dangerous markup from a feed item is stripped/escaped would have caught this.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` every example stubs behavior around `execute` and explicitly asserts `poll_feed` is never/once called, but there are no specs that exercise `PollFeed#poll_feed` itself (the actual parsing loop and `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` followed by `TopicEmbed.import(...)`). In the diff, that path ultimately creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (via `TopicEmbed.import` -> `PostCreator`), and there is no sanitization/escaping in `PollFeed#poll_feed` or `TopicEmbed.import`. Therefore, the risky code path is indeed uncovered by tests, and a test expecting dangerous markup to be stripped/escaped would currently fail (or would need implementation) and would have caught this gap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly marks “\ No newline at end of file” for multiple newly added files (e.g., embed.css.scss, embed/loading.html.erb, layouts/embed.html.erb, lib/topic_retriever.rb), so the observation is factually correct. However, missing a trailing newline is a formatting/style nit and not a functional bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the code.
